first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independently consolidated memories (86, 31) point to onboarding/signup simplification as a durable driver of activation and time-to-value in self-serve accounts—directly addressing the observed metric decay. I verify these two before committing since they most directly justify this week's single experiment slot. I deliberately avoid promotional_pricing despite competitive pressure: memory_73 was consolidated under different market conditions (proactive pricing test, not a reactive price war against an aggressive new entrant), and matching competitor pricing risks eroding long-term unit economics and training price-sensitive segments to churn-shop, undermining the sustainable qualified revenue objective. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentive memories don't address the acute onboarding/activation regression. Given only guarded confidence in how well the original onboarding results generalize to the current funnel state, I'm scoping this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, preserving room to reassess if pricing pressure continues to bite before next week's slot.
